input.quote: 11.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years.
input.rationale: Section 11 locks us into a five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals, and Section 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. There is no convenience exit for Corio (the customer) at any point during the multi-year term, and no refund mechanism for prepaid license or support fees, which the playbook treats as a missing-behaviour deviation for terms longer than 12 months. We added a new Section 11.4 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund and no early-termination penalty, while confirming Commerce One has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right.

proposal.summary: Add Corio convenience termination right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The five-year term gives us no way out except for Commerce One's breach, so we added a convenience exit on thirty (30) days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid license and support fees. If a longer runway is needed we can move to sixty (60) days' notice, but we cannot commit for five years with no termination right.

ops.text: 11.4 Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, without payment of any early termination fee, penalty or other charge, in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio, within thirty (30) days of the effective date of termination, any prepaid license, support or maintenance fees allocable to the period after such effective date. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term.
